We understand that you may feel frustrated, however the tone and comments within your message about our staff are not acceptable.

Our reception team follow a clinically-led triage process and do not make decisions about your care, these are made by qualified clinicians to ensure patients are prioritised safely and appropriately.

At the time of your request, your symptoms were assessed as non-urgent and a routine appointment was offered. We very rarely offer telephone appointments, so this would have been selected as the most appropriate way for a clinician to review your concerns initially.

We have some of the best access in the city. This is achieved through robust clinical assessment and carefully matching patient need to available clinical capacity, ensuring those who need urgent care are seen promptly.

Your comment that there are “no patients in the centre” is not accurate. Our waiting room is consistently busy throughout the day, aside from the lunch period.

We will not tolerate disrespectful or abusive comments towards our staff.

If you would like this reviewed further, I am happy to listen to the call to ensure the correct process has been followed. Please email standrewsmc.ooh@nhs.net with further details so this can be investigated.

Leaving a 1-star review in these circumstances can come across as a reflection of frustration rather than an accurate representation of the service provided.

We would always encourage patients to raise concerns directly with the practice so they can be properly reviewed and addressed.

If you feel that our service does not meet your expectations, you are free to register with an alternative GP practice.

If your symptoms worsen or change, please contact us again so that we can reassess.

Regards

Moreover, it is absolutely ridiculous that you have to divulge incredibly personal information to a receptionist as an *attempt* to get an appointment, which on the same day is highly unlikely.

I have never experienced such a poor system, where receptionists are entitled to ask for such sensitive information and with a lack of medical training, then determine if they personally think your condition warrants seeing a GP that same day. No one should feel so embarrassed walking into their GP practice, knowing that the receptionists are aware of the extremely personal details of your visit nor should patients have to listen whilst people requesting appointments at the desk are forced to divulge such details in front of the entire waiting area.

Patients should not be vetted as a mere attempt at receiving an appointment on the same day regardless of whether it’s over the phone or in person.

ZERO TOLERANCE
The Practice takes it very seriously if a member of staff or one of the doctors or nursing team is treated in an abusive or violent way.

The Practice supports the government's 'Zero Tolerance' campaign for Health Service Staff. This states that GPs and their staff have a right to care for others without fear of being attacked or abused. To successfully provide these services a mutual respect between all the staff and patients has to be in place. All our staff aim to be polite, helpful, and sensitive to all patients’ individual needs and circumstances. They would respectfully remind patients that very often staff could be confronted with a multitude of varying and sometimes difficult tasks and situations, all at the same time.  The staff understand that ill patients do not always act in a reasonable manner and will take this into consideration when trying to deal with a misunderstanding or complaint.

However, aggressive behaviour, be it violent or abusive, will not be tolerated and may result in you being removed from the Practice list and, in extreme cases, the Police being contacted.

You had already received a warning letter in the weeks prior to your removal and your behaviour was not an isolated incident.

A good patient-doctor relationship, based on mutual respect and trust, is the cornerstone of good patient care. The removal of patients from our list is an exceptional and rare event and is a last resort in an impaired patient-practice relationship. I was contacted a very long time ago.
In relation to the allegation i swore at a member of staff that tried to help me - this is absolutely untrue, as two children were present and I would NEVER swear at someone else anyway, I was brought up better than that, this will be recorded then?

After 29 years, since birth, that I have been registered at the surgery, I have felt
no other option than to go elsewhere.
There are many things that an individual based on their own experiences can find upsetting, stressful and these things can be minor to someone else.
18 months ago my daughter was treated for sepsis after a water infection. The hospital
And community nurses really drummed into me the importance of the signs of infection and to act on them at the earliest convenience.
There was a recent accident that caused my 2YO daughter to get an injury to her hand, it required a recent A&E trip. At A&E after lots of
X-rays she was allowed home I was told
The importance of keeping a close eye on it, any changes must be reported to the GP
For further advice.

Yesterday after spending a couple
Of days worried about it, I took her to the chemist and was told it needed advice from
A GP & to contact them which I did. I feel it really matters who you speak to at St Andrews as to what the outcome is , I was told “I can assure you that the dr won’t see you for a sore finger.” I didn’t want her to be seen if I could help it, given the nature of the current pandemic, I simply just wanted advice.it took a call
To 111 to finally get the Drs  Reception staff to pass a message on to the GP & After finally speaking to a Dr, I sent him a picture and he agreed it was infected and she needed antibiotics.

A couple of years ago I received some results from a smear that were slightly worrying and my smear test was due this year in lockdown. It was booked in and then cancelled and then I had discovered they were rebooked in but I wasn’t contacted.
I saw a post on the Facebook page, I commented asking why I wasn’t contacted and if I was able to book in. I received a very rude and unprofessional reply back to me, with some “eye roll” emojis and then was blocked from the page.
It seems that the surgery cannot tolerate any comments that are not 100% praising to their staff.

After this I did send a complaint via the website about the unprofessional attitude I had experienced and never heard back.
I was recently told by a member of reception staff “if i was that bothered Id have gone to A&E.”

The surgery isn’t accessible for wider Pram’s and as I do have a wider Pram for my children I have never had a problem anywhere since I’ve had it. It means that appointments for my children have had to happen with the door open and my Pram
In the corridor. A member of staff was asked to stand with one of my children  in the corridor while we discussed a sensitive issue with my other child in the Drs room. as my daughter began to cry as she wondered where I was going, the member of staff said to me “you should have brought her a toy she’ll Scream the place down now the whole appointment.” It’s a nice comment to make to a mum already feeling the stress of three young children already feeling anxious about her child crying. When I rang up about this when I got home
And asked what other people in this situation do, I was told some staff aren’t “children people”
And was given the name of another girl to ask for if I needed to bring the Pram in the future.

I have tried to contact the practise about the issues and have never found them to be acknowledged, but I have ALWAYS been the first to thank and praise staff for their help when it’s been positive experience for me.

I do hope this review is acknowledged so that there are never other parents or young people who feel anxious about smear tests, who, maybe don’t have the support I have around me, aren’t left to feel how I have felt recently.
This time especially when there isn’t the same support from other service such as health visitors.",null,[0,200]]]],[null,1605889285000000,1605889285000000,"5 years ago",null,"https://business.google.com/local/business/4318677830778845355/customers/reviews/reply?p=CiRDaGREU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZKUTBGblNVTnBYemQ1U3pkblJSQUIQAA%3D%3D",[null,null,null,"/local/business/4318677830778845355/customers/reviews/reply?p=CiRDaGREU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZKUTBGblNVTnBYemQ1U3pkblJSQUIQAA%3D%3D"],"https://business.google.com/local/business/4318677830778845355/customers/reviews/deletereply?p=CiRDaGREU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZKUTBGblNVTnBYemQ1U3pkblJSQUIQAA%3D%3D",[null,null,null,"/local/business/4318677830778845355/customers/reviews/deletereply?p=CiRDaGREU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZKUTBGblNVTnBYemQ1U3pkblJSQUIQAA%3D%3D"],null,"https://business.google.com/local/business/4318677830778845355/customers/reviews/reply?p=CiRDaGREU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZKUTBGblNVTnBYemQ1U3pkblJSQUIQAA%3D%3D",[null,null,null,"/local/business/4318677830778845355/customers/reviews/reply?p=CiRDaGREU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZKUTBGblNVTnBYemQ1U3pkblJSQUIQAA%3D%3D"],null,["en"],[["Zoe

originally wrote a 5/5 review when I first joined this practice because my first impressions were good.

However, as with most, time and hands on experience reveal things for what they truly are; and I’m sad to report that this is the second GP practice in the area to let me down and leave me in a worse position than when I registered as a patient.

I’m not entirely sure whether I should pinpoint my frustration down to the practice manager who consistently failed to resolve my concerns and persistently refused to arrange a meeting; or the doctors who left my diagnosis and appointments in limbo for over 12 months, failed to provide any meaningful support or treatment, and ultimately had the indecency of kicking me out of the practice after being patient for over a year and then complaining because my frustrations grew (without being resolved).

A practice representative will likely reply to this comment saying they believe they did all they could, or try to pin the blame on me as the individual by insinuating I was a problematic patient (like they seem to with all other negative feedback); however, I disagree wholly. I counted over 30 appointments discussing the same or worsening symptoms; with absolutely no change in outcome or treatment offered. Despite receiving multiple diagnosis from hospitals, new findings from scan reports, and needing follow up with certain specialities - doctors at this practice repeatedly told me that they were ‘writing letters’ to consultants and hospitals to ‘chase them up’. It’s all recorded that during multiple appointments with at least 3 different doctors: all of them have said they are writing a letter and chasing up consultants for a follow up. Yet 12 months later they’re still writing the same letters and still haven’t developed the initiative to be a little more proactive and urgent about the issue. How many appointments is it reasonable to attend and be told that they’re writing the exact same letter as the previous doctor wrote a month ago or so, before somebody realises how futile their letter writing attempts are? This is also forgetting that for at least one referral, I found out that I wasn’t actually referred — resulting in many months wasted thinking I was in a queue.

Understandably, covid-19 has been a massive barrier and caused many issues for the NHS; however I don’t believe these delays and lack of direction in my care or treatment can be blamed on coronavirus. My healthcare stagnated and actually declined whilst being registered here, and I truly didn’t think that any practice could be as bad as my previous one. I’m genuinely sad to learn that I am wrong.

It’s far too easy for practices to do the absolute bare minimum (if anything at all) and then claim the patient-doctor relationship has broken down when you complain. I’m not sure how fair or legal that is - but each to their own! I’d like to think patients are protected from complaining and expressing their concerns and frustrations without fear of being kicked out - however that is definitely NOT the case.

Hopefully my experience does not put other patients off from registering here; but instead serves as a warning and feedback as to how you could’ve better handled my care and dealt with this whole situation much more efficiently; ultimately causing as little stress as possible for all parties. It’s clear to me that this has resulted in an unfavourable outcome for all; one which I believe could have been very easily avoided with a little cooperation from the practice manager and doctors. I was more than willing to meet to discuss my concerns in full from the moment I started encountering them & believe that it’s through no fault of my own that my concerns grew into larger problems.

All in all, a similarly disappointing and distressing patient experience as my previous GP practice. Perhaps most upsetting is how during my first appointment with a doctor, i was promised that he would trawl my medical notes and put a stop to my diagnosis-limbo and   decide an appropriate course of action. He never did.",null,[0,105]]]],[null,1604479927000000,1604479927000000,"5 years ago",null,"https://business.google.com/local/business/4318677830778845355/customers/reviews/reply?p=CiRDaGREU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZKUTBGblNVTnBkblEyYjJwblJSQUIQAA%3D%3D",[null,null,null,"/local/business/4318677830778845355/customers/reviews/reply?p=CiRDaGREU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZKUTBGblNVTnBkblEyYjJwblJSQUIQAA%3D%3D"],"https://business.google.com/local/business/4318677830778845355/customers/reviews/deletereply?p=CiRDaGREU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZKUTBGblNVTnBkblEyYjJwblJSQUIQAA%3D%3D",[null,null,null,"/local/business/4318677830778845355/customers/reviews/deletereply?p=CiRDaGREU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZKUTBGblNVTnBkblEyYjJwblJSQUIQAA%3D%3D"],null,"https://business.google.com/local/business/4318677830778845355/customers/reviews/reply?p=CiRDaGREU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZKUTBGblNVTnBkblEyYjJwblJSQUIQAA%3D%3D",[null,null,null,"/local/business/4318677830778845355/customers/reviews/reply?p=CiRDaGREU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZKUTBGblNVTnBkblEyYjJwblJSQUIQAA%3D%3D"],null,["en"],[["Thank you for your feedback Ben.
